title: The Attractive Economics Behind Anthropic Data Center Sprint
source_used: Chosunbiz English (12 Oct 2026), relaying The Information; The Information page is paywalled and gave only its description
key_facts: The Information reported on 11 Oct 2026 that Anthropic signed a multi-year cloud contract with the neocloud company IREN; size and term were not disclosed.
Anthropic has also signed data centre leasing contracts totalling more than 15 GW across over 10 clouds, including AWS and Google, worth about $530 billion.
Anthropic's computing capacity is expected to rise from 1.4 GW last year to 5 GW this year, 9.5 GW next year and more than 15 GW in 2028.

The Information says the reason for the rush is that the faster servers come online, the more revenue they generate: by investor and analyst estimates, if Anthropic uses all of a 245 MW leased Louisiana data centre for inference (answering requests) and starts one month earlier than planned, it could add $1.3 billion in sales.
The Louisiana site is developed by Hut 8 and operated by Fluidstack and will run Google TPUs from the second quarter of next year.
Occam Edge estimates gross margin could reach 85 percent if Anthropic spends about $200 million a month renting the facility's chips, excluding training and labour costs.
The Information said Anthropic recorded a small profit in the second quarter; its margin could decline as leasing grows, and competition with OpenAI is intensifying.
quote_evidence: U.S. IT outlet The Information reported on the 11th (local time) that Anthropic signed a multi-year cloud contract with IREN.
The Information analyzed that the reason Anthropic is rushing to secure and activate data centers is that the faster the servers are brought online, the more massive revenue they can generate.
why_it_matters_hint: Anthropic is racing to bring leased computing power online because each month saved could be worth over a billion dollars at one site, by outside estimates.
notes: The Information page returned HTTP 200 but no article body (paywall); its page description confirms the $530 billion of leasing deals and the speed-up theme. Facts come from Chosunbiz's English account of the report. Figures are investor and analyst estimates under stated assumptions.
